name: Epaphras
title: Founder of the Colossian Church
summary: Epaphras was a faithful coworker of the apostle Paul and the founder of the church in Colossae. He was known for his intense prayer on behalf of the churches in the Lycus Valley and was highly regarded by Paul for his service and dedication to the gospel.

keyEvents.title: Founded the church in Colossae
keyEvents.description: Epaphras preached the gospel and established the church in Colossae, likely while Paul was in Ephesus. He taught the Colossians about God's grace in truth.

keyEvents.title: Brought a report to Paul
keyEvents.description: Epaphras traveled to Rome to tell Paul about the condition of the church and the challenges they faced with false teaching.

keyEvents.title: Earnest intercession for the churches
keyEvents.description: Epaphras was known for his fervent prayer for the believers in Colossae, Laodicea, and Hierapolis, that they might stand firm and complete in God's will.

keyEvents.title: Fellow prisoner with Paul
keyEvents.description: Epaphras is referred to as Paul's fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus, showing his dedication to the gospel even under difficult circumstances.
